_comment: Endpoints for run_benchmark.py. API keys come from the environment -- never commit one.
Every hosted model below is on the PUBLIC NVIDIA API catalog at
integrate.api.nvidia.com, reachable by anyone with a free NGC personal API key
from build.nvidia.com. That is deliberate: this sample has to be reproducible by
people outside NVIDIA, so it does not use any NVIDIA-internal inference service.
If you work at NVIDIA and want to use an internal one instead, copy this file,
change base_url, and keep the copy local -- endpoints-*.json is gitignored for
exactly that.
Model ids are the catalog's own, as shown on each build.nvidia.com model card.
Internal services generally use different ids, carrying a provider prefix.
Concurrency is deliberately low: an earlier sweep at concurrency 4 tripped a
gateway rate limit and four of eight models returned HTTP 429 on every call.
The free catalog tier is rate limited too, so keep this modest.
max_tokens, concurrency and timeout are all per-endpoint. Free-tier catalog
endpoints queue: one measured 264 s to return 17 tokens, which is wait rather
than generation. For those, raise concurrency to overlap the waits and raise
timeout so a queue length is not mistaken for a dead model. Lowering max_tokens
does not help when the time is spent queueing.
max_attempts is the retry budget per request. Free-tier endpoints rate-limit on
request count; the runner honours Retry-After when the gateway sends it, and
never retries a 400 -- a malformed request fails the same way eight times.

endpoints.name: spark
endpoints._note: Matched to nemotron-hosted so the local-vs-hosted control is a fair one. At the 3072 default this reasoning model exhausted its budget on three examples: a correct decision, but no tool call and no text, which reads as a silent failure and understates the local result.

endpoints.name: nemotron-hosted
endpoints._note: The control: same model as the Spark endpoint, someone else's hardware.

endpoints.name: gemma-4-31b
endpoints._note: Dense 31B. Latency on the free tier is bimodal -- measured at both 1.7 s and 264 s for the same trivial request, so the slow case is queueing rather than compute. Concurrency 4 absorbs a queue without bursting hard against a shared endpoint.

endpoints.name: kimi-k3
endpoints._note: Rate limits on request count, so concurrency does not buy throughput. Left at 2 with a deeper retry budget: one of six failed in the smoke run, and a complete row is worth the wall-clock time.
